build: PAL original, two-sided G64; level 1 load in play

comments.text: Entry of the level 2 file, jumped to by the resident loader at $0424. Jumps straight to the main loop at $1FC4, which first runs the level setup at $5335.
Non-maskable interrupt: sets the flag $0A2B to 1 and returns. The main loop at $2010 reads the flag.
Set to 1 by every NMI ($0A23); cleared by the level setup at $53C1 and read by the main loop at $2010.
Sprite pointer value of each slot, 14 bytes ($0A32-$0A3F); written by the behaviours and copied into both screens' pointer tables by the multiplexer $6604.
Sprite colour of each slot, 14 bytes; written by the behaviours and copied to $D02A and on by $6604.
1 when a slot's sprite is multicolour, 14 bytes; $6604 copies it into $D01C.
Animation counter of each slot, 14 bytes, stepped by the behaviours that animate ($1457, $15F2, $1ADD, $1BAF, $1E06, $14F4).
Walk phase 0 to $1F of each slot, 14 bytes, which picks the frame from the tables at $1747, $1767, $1982 and $19A2.
Frames left in the current random walk of each slot, 14 bytes; set from $65AE in $1787 and $19C2.

Hurt timer of each slot, 14 bytes: set to 10 by $10B2, counted down by $1787 and $19C2 before the enemy walks or starts a shot again. Their close-attack test runs before the timer is tested, so a hurt enemy can still attack.

State of each of the 11 slots (14 bytes): 0 free, 1 and 2 walking, 3 to 13 the other behaviours (7 the second half of an enemy, handled through $1D3E), 14 and 15 attacking, 16 knocked down, 17 an enemy's shot; picks the routine in the table at $128B.
Type and state of each of the 84 objects; 0 means no object, and the value is copied into $0A94 when the object takes a slot.
The table at $0AA2 read from two entries on: the type of the object two after the one in Y, which $1787 and $19C2 compare with $11.
The rest of the table at $0AA2 as it is read from two entries on (see $0AA4).
The counter table at $0AFF read one entry back; $1C94 sets it to 7 for the object before the one in Y.
Counter of each object, used by the behaviours as a timer, step or saved state (copied from $921A at the start).
The counter table at $0AFF read one entry on; $61AC sets it to $FE when an enemy is knocked down and $6273 counts it down.
The counter table at $0AFF read two entries on; $1809 and $1A43 test it and $1718 and $1953 set it to $32.
The rest of the counter table at $0AFF as it is read two entries on (see $0B01).
Flag of each object: set to 1 by $1817 and $1A51 when an enemy starts an attack from a distance (probably a shot) and cleared at $1713 and $194E; copied from $926D at the start.

Energy of each object: each hit by the player takes 2 off it ($61AC, which never goes below 0), and a hit that finds it at 0 knocks the enemy down; $6273 sets it to 3 when the enemy gets up. For pickups it is set to 1 when taken. Copied from $92C0.
Variant flag of each object, 0 or 1 (a second set of frames and attack steps; the colour code tests it too, but stores the same colour 0 for both in this level); copied from $9313.
A flag of each object: 1 keeps an enemy standing with its first frame until the hit test $10B2 sets it to 2 (read at $1796 and $19D1); 0 and 2 let it act. Copied from $9366.
Left limit of the object's walk, low byte, for each of the 84 objects; copied from $93B9. For a shot (type $11) it is the direction instead: 0 right, otherwise left ($12D5).
The table at $0C9E read two entries on; $170E sets it to 1 and $1949 to 0 for the object two after the one in Y.
The rest of the table at $0C9E as it is read two entries on (see $0CA0).
Left limit of the object's walk, high byte; copied from $940C.
Right limit of the object's walk, low byte; copied from $945F.
Right limit of the object's walk, high byte; copied from $94B2.

The table at $0DEA read one entry back: the world X, low byte, of the object before the one in Y; $138B and $1572 restore a falling or shooting object to it, and $1C98 places its object $16 pixels to the left of it.
World X of each object, low byte; copied from $9505 and kept up to date by the behaviours.
The table at $0DEA read one entry on; the walking behaviours and the hit test $10B2 store the new X here as well as in $0DEA.
The table at $0DEA read two entries on: $171D and $1958 store there the X of the enemy that starts a shot.
The rest of the table at $0DEA as it is read two entries on (see $0DEC).
The table at $0E3D read one entry back: the world X, high byte, of the object before the one in Y.
World X of each object, high byte; copied from $9558.
The table at $0E3D read one entry on; the walking behaviours and the hit test $10B2 store the new high byte here too.
The table at $0E3D read two entries on: $1722 and $195D store there the high byte of the X of a shot.
The rest of the table at $0E3D as it is read two entries on (see $0E3F).
The table at $0E90 read one entry back: the world Y, low byte, of the object before the one in Y.
World Y of each object, low byte; copied from $95AB.
The table at $0EE3 read one entry back: the world Y, high byte, of the object before the one in Y.
World Y of each object, high byte; copied from $95FE.
The object each of the slots holds (14 bytes), set by $0FA5 and cleared by the setup $52B6.
The table at $0F44 read one entry back: the slot held by the object before the one in Y, which $1D3E, $796D and $79D6 use to find the other half of an enemy.
The slot each object holds, for the 84 objects; set by $0FA5 and cleared by the setup $52B6.
Scratch bytes of $0FA5: the difference between an object and the camera, across ($0F9E/$0F9F) and down ($0FA0/$0FA1).
High byte of the horizontal distance between an object and the camera in $0FA5.
Low byte of the vertical distance between an object and the camera in $0FA5.
High byte of the vertical distance between an object and the camera in $0FA5.
Target of the beq at $0FAA in scan_objects: a short hop on to the release code at $1033, because a branch cannot reach it.

Scans the 84 objects, last to first (X from $53), against the camera ($FB/$FC across, $FD/$FE down). An object with type $0AA2 of 0, or outside the window (from 26 pixels left of the camera to $0159 right of it, and $14 to $C2 below the camera's height) is released: its slot in $0A94 is cleared, the high byte of the slot's Y ($CD) set to $FE and its flag $1056 cleared. One inside the window that has no slot yet takes the first free slot of the 11 ($0A94 zero), receives its position and type, and $0F36/$0F44 link slot and object; when no slot is free the scan stops there until the next call.
Holds the X register saved by $1038: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1048, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
1 for each object that holds a slot, 84 bytes; set and cleared by $0FA5, and cleared for every object by the setup $52B6.
Set to 1 by $10B2 when it lands a hit, which makes further calls of $10B2 return at once; cleared by the player routines at $5BC7 and $5D91.
Set to 1 by $10B2 on a hit, with $10B0; cleared by the player routine at $5BCA. $61AC reads it to take 2 instead of 1 from the object's energy.

For slot X (object Y), when no hit has been scored since the player last walked or fell ($10B0, $10B1, cleared by $5BC7 and $5D91), the player is striking ($5BBA or $5B2C set) and the slot is in state 1, 2, 14 or 15: compares the slot's height ($A3,X) with the player's ($747C) (up to 9 lines below it or $17 above) and its distance across with $747B, on the side the player faces ($59B9). On a hit it pushes the object 9 pixels away along the map unless it is past its limit ($0C9E-$0D97), sets the slot to state 1 (player facing right) or 2 (facing left), starts the hurt timer $0A86 with 10, sets $10B0 and $10B1 and calls $61AC.
Number of state 7 slots queued in $1206 by $1214.
List of the slots in state 7 found by $1214 (ended by $FF), handled after the others by $1D3E.

Per-frame object update, skipped while the game is paused ($6443). Goes through the 11 slots: a slot in state 7 is only queued in the list at $1206; for the others, while the raster is above line $B4, it runs the player-attack test $10B2 and then the behaviour for the slot's state, through the table at $128B and a call whose operand is rewritten at $125F/$1260. The queued state 7 slots are then handled by $1D3E.
operand $125F/$1260 rewritten from the table at $128B; $12AF shown is the value left in the file
Low byte of the address in the JSR at $125E, rewritten by $1252 with the routine for the current case, so the call goes to a different routine each time.
High byte of the address in the JSR at $125E, rewritten by $1258 with the routine for the current case, so the call goes to a different routine each time.
Holds the X register saved by $1275: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1283, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
The object of the slot being handled by $1214 ($0F36,X), which the behaviours and $10B2 use as Y.

Table of the 18 behaviour routines, one word each, indexed by the slot state in $0A94 times 2: 0 $12AF (an RTS), 1 $1787, 2 $19C2, 3 $1ADD, 4 $1BAF, 5 $1C01, 6 $1C1C, 7 $1D3E, 8 $1E06, 9 $15F2, 10 $1457, 11 $14F4, 12 $133E, 13 $1344, 14 $1895, 15 $1659, 16 $6273, 17 $12B0 (the word at $12AD).
The high bytes of the words of the behaviour table at $128B (every second byte).
A lone RTS, the behaviour of a free slot (state 0).

Behaviour for state 17, the last word of the behaviour table at $128B: the shot a walking enemy fires, with frames $73 and $74, the two short dashes of dash_shapes. Five objects of the level table ($91BD) have type $11, each two places after a walking enemy, and $0FA5 copies that type into $0A94. Sets the sprite colour $0A40 to $0B (dark grey) and the frame $0A32 to 0. While the counter $0AFF of the object is not 0 it takes 1 off the counter, tests the slot against the player ($5507) and, on contact, hurts the player ($5579), sets the counter to 0 and returns. Without contact it moves the slot 5 pixels a call, to the right with the frame $73 when the byte $0C9E of the object (obj_left_lo) is 0 and to the left with the frame $74 otherwise, and copies the new X to the object ($0DEA and $0E3D). The counter is set to 0 when the slot's screen position $BF is negative, when it moves right with $BF at 1 or more and $87 at $28 or more, or when it moves left with $BF at 0 and $87 below $14. With the counter at 0 it puts the slot and the object at the X of the object two places before it, the enemy ($0DE8 and $0E3B). The enemy's attack starts the shot: $1659 and $1895 set its counter to $32, its direction byte $0C9E (1 left, 0 right) and its X.
Behaviour for state 12: sets the sprite colour $0A40 to 6 and does nothing else.

Behaviour for state 13: moves 3 pixels left a frame while the height follows the table at $13AC (16-bit steps) over $64 frames, then puts the object back at the position of the previous object. The steps fall faster and faster and then turn upward, four times, so it is probably a bouncing object. No object of level 2's table ($91BD) starts in state 13.
Height steps of the falling object of behaviour $1344, 16 bits each, indexed by twice the count in $0AFF (which runs to 99); the first 78 steps end at $1447, where the next table starts.
The high bytes of the 16-bit height steps at $13AC (every second byte).

Steps 32 to 77 of fall_steps ($13AC), the last 46 of its 78 height steps (16 bits each, low byte first, signed): 2 for 1 entry, 3 for 2 entries, 4 for 2 entries, 5 for 2 entries, -4 for 2 entries, -3 for 2 entries, -2 for 2 entries, -1 for 2 entries, 0 for 2 entries, 1 for 2 entries, 2 for 2 entries, 3 for 2 entries, -2 for 2 entries, -1 for 2 entries, 0 for 2 entries, 1 for 2 entries, -1 for 2 entries, 0 for 13 entries. The first 32 steps are at $13AC. The count in $0AFF that indexes the table runs to 99, so the counts 78 to 99 read the bytes after the end of the table at $1447.
The 15 sprite pointer values ($68 seven times, then $69 eight times) of the shuttling object of behaviour $1457, indexed by $0A5C.

Behaviour for state 10: moves the object back and forth between its two limits ($0C9E-$0CF1 and $0D44-$0D97), 2 pixels a frame, with the direction in $0AFF and the frame from $1448. It makes no contact test.
Holds the Y register saved by $146F: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1479, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Eight steps of 4 bytes of the shooter of behaviour $14F4: change in X and in Y, 16 bits each, indexed by 4 times $0A5C.
The second byte of each shot step in the table at $14D0: the change in X, high byte.
The third byte of each shot step in the table at $14D0: the change in Y, low byte.
The fourth byte of each shot step in the table at $14D0: the change in Y, high byte.
Working copy of the change in X, low byte, of the current step of the shot in $14F4.
Working copy of the change in X, high byte, of the current step of the shot in $14F4.
Working copy of the change in Y, low byte, of the current step of the shot in $14F4.
Working copy of the change in Y, high byte, of the current step of the shot in $14F4.

Behaviour for state 11: a shot fired from the object before it (in level 2 a shuttle of state 10). It hurts the player on contact; otherwise, while the counter $0AFF is not 0, it takes 1 off and moves by one step of the table at $14D0 (4 bytes each: across and down, 16 bits), the step chosen by $0A5C, so each shot flies straight. When the counter is 0, or after a contact, it restarts the shot: counter $1E, $0A5C on to the next of the eight directions, the slot back at the position of the object before it, and sound effect 7 (X = $1C). A shot lasts $1F calls.
Holds the Y register saved by $1516: the immediate operand of the LDY at $153D, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the Y register saved by $1589: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1591, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $1586: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1593, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
The 90 sprite pointer values of the animated hazard of behaviour $15F2, indexed by $0A5C.

Behaviour for state 9: an animated hazard that hurts the player on contact while it is shown. Steps the counter $0A5C down from $5A and shows the frame from the table at $1596; when that frame is 0 (hidden) it makes no contact test.
Holds the Y register saved by $160A: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1614, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.

Returns 1 in A when the high byte $BF of slot X's screen X is not 0 (X past 255, or negative) or its screen X $87 is at or beyond the player's ($747B), and 0 otherwise; the walking behaviours use it to decide when to turn.
Returns 0 in A when slot X's screen height ($A3,X) is within nine lines above or $1B below the player's ($747C), and 1 when it is not.

Hit recoil counter, set to 3 by $5579 and to 4 by the enemy attacks and counted down by $6315; while it runs and the hurt guard $5577 is 0 the stored joystick byte is not refreshed. In practice that is after an enemy attack: $5579 sets $5577 to 3 as well, so the joystick is still read after it.

Behaviour for state 15: the attack of an enemy that was walking left, started by $1787. Counts $0AFF down from $19 and returns to state 1 at zero. At $18 it shows a frame, at $12 it steps 2 pixels left, at $0E it shows the attack frame and steps 6 left and then, when the player is within $1C in front of it, writes joystick left into $2064, sets the recoil $1658 to 4 and calls $5586, and launches its shot when $0B52 is set; at 4 it shows the walk frame and steps 8 back. Frames and offsets differ by the variant flag $0BF8 (operands patched at the start).
Immediate operand of the LDA at $16B2, set by $1660 and $1681 to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the ADC at $16BA, set by $1665 and $1686 to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the LDA at $16C9, set by $166A and $168B to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the SBC at $16D1, set by $166F and $1690 to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the SBC at $172D, set by $1674 and $1695 to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the LDA at $1741, set by $1679 and $169A to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
The 32 sprite pointer values of an enemy walking left (variant 0), indexed by the phase $0A6A.
The 32 sprite pointer values of an enemy walking left (variant 1), indexed by the phase $0A6A.

Behaviour for state 1: probably an enemy walking left. Waits out the hurt timer $0A86, walks one pixel left in runs of random length ($0A78 from $65AE) and turns (state 2) when it reaches its left limit ($0C9E/$0CF1) or when a new run starts while it is left of the player ($1626); when the player is near on its left it switches to state 15 (attack), even while hurt, and when the object two after it is a shot (type $11) it may start that attack at random to fire it. Sprite frames come from $1747 or $1767 by the variant flag $0BF8.

Behaviour for state 14: the mirror of $1659, for an enemy that was walking right, started by $19C2. Counts $0AFF down, returns to state 2 at zero, and in reach of the player writes joystick right into $2064, sets $1658 to 4 and calls $5586.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $18EE, set by $189C and $18BD to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the SBC at $18F6, set by $18A1 and $18C2 to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the LDA at $1905, set by $18A6 and $18C7 to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the ADC at $190D, set by $18AB and $18CC to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).
Immediate operand of the ADC at $1968, set by $18B0 and $18D1 to the value for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 (the attack frame, step size or offset).

Immediate operand of the LDA at $197C, set by $18B5 and $18D6 to the sprite frame for the enemy variant given by the flag $0BF8 ($12 for variant 1, $02 for variant 0); the STA at $197E puts it in $0A32 when the count reaches $18.
The 32 sprite pointer values of an enemy walking right (variant 0), indexed by the phase $0A6A.
The 32 sprite pointer values of an enemy walking right (variant 1), indexed by the phase $0A6A.

Behaviour for state 2: probably an enemy walking right, the mirror of $1787. Walks one pixel right in random runs to its right limit ($0D44/$0D97), turns into state 1 there, and goes to state 14 (attack) when the player is near on its right. Frames from $1982 or $19A2.
The sprite pointer values of the pickup of behaviour $1ADD, indexed by $0A5C (0 to 11): 14 bytes, $62 seven times and $63 seven times, of which the 12 read are $62 seven times and $63 five times.

Behaviour for state 3, probably an energy pickup. Bobs along the path in $1B66 with frames from $1ACF, and when the player touches it ($5507) sets its done flag $0BA5, adds 10 to the energy $5578 (a result of $18 or more becomes $21, the full bar) and plays sound effect 4 (X = $10) through $B0EE.
Holds the Y register saved by $1B05: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1B0F, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the Y register saved by $1B59: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1B61, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $1B56: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1B63, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Height steps of the pickup of behaviour $1ADD, 16 bits each, 24 entries, indexed by $0AFF, which steps by 2 from 0 to $2E.
The high bytes of the 16-bit height steps at $1B66 (every second byte).
The 25 sprite pointer values of the pickup of behaviour $1BAF, indexed by $0A5C.
Behaviour for state 4, probably a bonus pickup. Cycles through the frames at $1B96 and, when touched, sets $0BA5, adds 5 to the score digit 4 ($585D) and plays sound effect 3 (X = $0C).
Holds the Y register saved by $1BD2: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1BDC, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the Y register saved by $1BF4: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1BFC, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $1BF1: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1BFE, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Behaviour for state 5: sets the sprite colour $0A40 to 0, then shows sprite $6B while the counter $0AFF counts down by one a call and sprite $6A once it is 0; it does nothing else.

Behaviour for state 6, probably a thrown or falling hazard. On contact with the player ($5507) it hurts him ($5579) and restarts. Otherwise it counts $0AFF up to $6A, moves 4 pixels left between counts 4 and $33, and moves in height by the table at $1CD1 (a value of $5A or more is used as the sprite frame instead). When the run ends it puts itself $16 pixels left of and 1 above the object before it, sets that object's counter $0AFE to 7, and plays sound effect 5 (X = $14).
Holds the Y register saved by $1CC4: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1CCC, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $1CC1: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1CCE, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Height steps of the hazard of behaviour $1C1C, one byte each, 106 entries; a value of $5A or more is a sprite pointer.

Entries 64 to 105, the last 42, of hazard_arc_steps ($1CD1). All are sprite pointers, which are the values of $5A or more: $64 for 5 entries, $65 for 5 entries, $66 for 5 entries, $64 for 5 entries, $65 for 5 entries, $66 for 5 entries, $71 for 6 entries, $72 for 6 entries. $64 to $66 are the three flames of flame_shapes, $71 is flame_small_shape and $72 is the first shape of dash_shapes.
The sprite pointer limit ($05 or $14, by the variant flag $0BF8) that $1D3E compares the linked slot's frame with.
The linked slot found by $1D3E, kept while it picks the sprite pointer.

Behaviour for a slot in state 7, run after the other slots by $1214. Sets the slot's X from its object and picks its sprite pointer by the sprite frame and phase $0A6A of the slot belonging to the previous object ($0F43): from $6219/$6255 when that slot is in state $10 (knocked down), otherwise from $1DDA or $1DBA, so probably the lower sprite of a two-sprite enemy that follows the upper one.
The 32 sprite pointer values of the following sprite of $1D3E, used when the linked slot's frame is at or above the limit; indexed by $0A6A.
The 32 sprite pointer values of the following sprite of $1D3E, used when the linked slot's frame is below the limit; indexed by $0A6A.
The 12 sprite pointer values of the hazard of behaviour $1E06, indexed by $0A5C.

Behaviour for state 8: a moving hazard that hurts the player on contact ($5507, $5579). Steps $0AFF by 2 up to $A0 and moves along the offsets in $1E82 (across) and $1F22 (down), with frames from $1DFA.
Holds the Y register saved by $1E23: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1E2D, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Steps across of the hazard of behaviour $1E06, 16 bits each, 80 entries, indexed by $0AFF, which steps by 2 from 0 to $9E.
The high bytes of the 16-bit steps across at $1E82 (every second byte).
Entries 32 to 79, the last 48, of hazard_path_x ($1E82), 16 bits each, low byte first, signed: -2 for 8 entries, 0 for 26 entries, 2 for 14 entries. The first 32 entries are at $1E82.
Steps down of the hazard of behaviour $1E06, 16 bits each, 80 entries.
The high bytes of the 16-bit steps down at $1F22 (every second byte).
Entries 32 to 79, the last 48, of hazard_path_y ($1F22), 16 bits each, low byte first, signed: 0 for 8 entries, 3 for 26 entries, 0 for 14 entries. The first 32 entries are at $1F22.
The player's world X, low byte; with $1FC3 the high byte, worked out by $7401 from the camera and $747B.
The player's world X, high byte, worked out by $7401 with $1FC2.

Starts play: runs the level setup $5335, then loops from $1FC7. Each pass calls $65CE (which returns at once), the object scan $0FA5, the energy bar $57D5, the level-end test $2050, the score digits $5889, the banner step $56D4, the timer routines $75FD and $755D, and the pause check $2029. When $0A11 is set, key code $20 in $8F44 ends the level; with $0A11 and the energy $5578 both zero it runs the death screen $8D6C, and the continue screen $8CBC while $0A12 is non-zero, which restarts the level when it sets $8CBB. The level ends through $201F (the wipe $74BC, then the loader at $0407) when $2060 is set; the NMI flag $0A2B sends it back to $0404 to load again from level 1.
Pause: when the key code in $8F44 is $50, sets $6443, waits for the key to be released, pressed again and released, then clears $6443.
Sets $2060 to 1 when the vertical scroll position in $FD/$FE is below $00B3, which makes the main loop at $200B end the level.
Set to 1 by $2050 when the vertical scroll position is in the end zone; the main loop then ends the level.
Horizontal fine scroll, ORed into the low bits of $D016 by $6480.
Vertical fine scroll, ORed into $D011 by $6480.

Joystick port 2 ($DC00) as read by $6315; bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire, clear when pressed. The enemy attacks at $16FC and $1937 overwrite it with a push to one side, which stays while $6315 skips its read during the recoil ($1658, $5577), and the setup at $537C sets it to $FF.
CIA 1 port B ($DC01) as last read by $6315.
Cleared by the level setup at $53C4; nothing else reads or writes it in this file.
Which of the two screen matrices is on show: 0 selects $CC00 and 1 selects $C800 (through $62FF); the scroll routines build the other one and flip this at the end.
The camera's height, low byte, saved by $206C before a scroll step and restored by the fine scroll routines.
The camera's height, high byte, saved by $206C before a scroll step.
The camera's X, low byte, saved by $206C before a scroll step and restored by the fine scroll routines.
The camera's X, high byte, saved by $206C before a scroll step.

Called by $63E8 each frame unless the banner flag $56D1 is set. When the game is paused ($6443) it only reads the keyboard ($2127). Otherwise it saves the camera ($FB-$FE) and the player position, then, from the player's screen position in $747B,$747C, picks one of eight scroll directions: right at X $DC or more, left below $64, up above Y $41, down at $87 or more (corners combine them); with none of these it only reads the keyboard. Second part of the unrolled colour lookup from the matrix at $C800: the characters from $CA04 on, stored in the buffer from $7197.
Last store of colours_c8_part2 before colours_c8_part3: puts the colour found in the colour table at $BF00 into colour_buffer at $720B. Named only so that the routine's 1,024-byte reach covers it.
Third part of the unrolled colour lookup from the matrix at $C800: the characters from $CA79 on, stored in the buffer from $720C.
Last store of colours_c8_part3 before colours_c8_part4: puts the colour found in the colour table at $BF00 into colour_buffer at $7280. Named only so that the routine's 1,024-byte reach covers it.
Last part of the unrolled colour lookup from the matrix at $C800: the characters up to $CAF6, stored in the buffer up to $7289, ending with the RTS at $52B5.

Copies the 84 entries of the 14 object tables from the level data at $91BD-$9650 into the working tables $0AA2-$0F36, clears the slot links $0F44 and active flags $1056, and zeroes six of the 14-byte slot tables: $0A5C, $0A78, $0A86, $0A94, $0F36 and $1206 (the phase table $0A6A is left as it is).

Level setup, called first by $1FC4. Banks the ROMs out ($01=$35), selects video bank 3 ($DD00 bits 0-1 cleared), screen at $CC00 ($D018=$30) with extended colour mode on, silences the sound ($B828), starts the countdown digits $755A-$755C (5 in $755C only when $0A10 is set), sets the energy $5578 to $21, clears the level flags and sprite registers, sets the player at $86,$6B and the camera X to $0032 and Y to $0484, the map pointer $A1/$A2 to $89BA. It then draws the briefing text ($903A, with the character-set swap $8FFF) and the panel ($54D6), loads the object tables ($52B6), draws the first screen ($73A3) and the panel again, sets up the sound-effect driver ($B0C8), points the NMI at $0A23 and the IRQ at $6315, sets the raster compare to line $82 and enables the raster interrupt with CLI.

Copies the status panel under the playfield: the 200 characters at $976E to $CEF7 and their colours at $9836 to $DAF7, clears the bottom row at $CFC0 and its colours at $DBC0 (40 bytes each), then draws the timer label through $760F when $0A10 is set. When $0A10 is clear it draws nothing more: the instruction at $54FC is an LDA of $7678, not a call, and $7678 is drawn only by $75FD when the timer runs out.
Scratch of $5507 (the player's height plus $0E) and of the hit tests $796D and $79D6 (the slot's height less $15).

Tests whether slot X overlaps the player: compares the slot's screen height ($A3,X) and position ($87,X, $BF,X) with the player's ($747C, $747B), with a height window that depends on the crouch flag $5B2D. Returns 0 in A for no overlap; for an overlap A is not 0 (the horizontal distance, or the slot's X when it equals the player's), and the callers test A against 0.
Frames of protection after a hit, set to 3 by $5579 and counted down by $6315.

The player's energy, $21 at the start of the level; the bar at $57D5 shows it, the pickup at $1ADD adds to it and $5586 takes from it. When it is zero and the cheat flag $0A11 is clear, the main loop shows the game-over screen ($8D6C) and, with credits left, the continue screen ($8CBC).
Takes one point of energy from the player unless the guard timer $5577 is running: sets $5577 and the recoil $1658 to 3, then falls into $5586.
Takes one point of energy from $5578 when it is not zero and plays sound effect 1 (X = $04) through $B0EE.
Holds the Y register saved by $5594: the immediate operand of the LDY at $559C, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $5591: the immediate operand of the LDX at $559E, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.

Called by $6480 while the banner flag $56D1 is set. Turns on all eight sprites, sets their colours and multicolours, and then busy-waits on the raster until line $96. Above line $63 it places the sprites as a block four across and two down (sprites 0-3 at height $3C, sprites 4-7 at $3C plus $15, pointers from $CB, through $5678), then above line $92 the same block at height $66 with pointers from $D3; from line $92 it puts six sprites at height $9B, with pointers from $C5 (through $5699), new X positions, colour 2 and multicolours 1 and 6, probably to draw a large picture across the screen. It sets the border to black before returning.
Part of the banner code: after a short delay, sets the heights of sprites 0-3 to A and of sprites 4-7 to A plus $15, then falls into $5699.
Sets the eight sprite pointers in both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFF and $CBF8-$CBFF) to X, X+1, up to X+7.
1 while the banner at $55A1 is on; set by $56D4.
Frames of the banner left; set to $C8 by $56D4.
Set to 1 by $56D4 once the banner has run, so that it does not start again.

Called by the main loop. Once only ($56D3 clear): when the high byte of the player's world X ($1FC3) is 2 or more and its low byte ($1FC2) is $22 or more, the camera's height is below $00E3 and the banner flag $56D1 is clear, it sets $56D1 and the countdown $56D2 to $C8 and blacks the first $2F8 bytes of colour RAM (rows 0 to 18, the play area). While $56D1 is set it counts $56D2 down and at 1 puts those colours back from the screen matrix ($2067 picks it) through the table at $BF00, clears $56D1 and sets $56D3.
The four masks $FC, $F0, $C0 and $00 that $57D5 uses to take pixels off the end of the bar.
64 bytes of shapes for the eight characters of the energy bar, built by $57D5 and copied to $FAC8.
Part of the energy bar shapes at $5794: byte 1 of the first character; $57D5 builds the pattern here.
Part of the energy bar shapes at $5794: byte 2 of the first character.
Part of the energy bar shapes at $5794: byte 3 of the first character.
Part of the energy bar shapes at $5794: byte 4 of the first character.
Part of the energy bar shapes at $5794: byte 5 of the first character.
The rest of the energy bar shapes at $5794: bytes 6 and 7 of the first character and the other seven characters.
Counter of $57D5: the energy step it has reached, counting up from $5578 to $21.

Builds the energy bar: fills 8 cells of the panel's screen matrix ($CF59 on) with the colours $1D and their colour RAM ($DB59) with 5, writes a striped pattern into bytes 1 to 6 of the eight 8-byte cells at $5794, masks off one multicolour pixel (two bits) for each step by which the energy $5578 is below $21, from the right-hand end (mask table at $5790), and copies the 64 bytes at $5794 to the panel bitmap at $FAC8.

Adds A to the decimal digit $0A00+X and carries towards the more significant digits (X counting down) until a digit does not overflow. Digit 6 is the units, so the 4 and 8 on digit 5 from $61AC are 40 and 80 points and the 5 on digit 4 at $1BAF is 500.
Scratch of $585D: the amount or carry added to the digit.
Draws the seven digits from $0A00 on into the panel bitmap's cells at $FA58 (8 bytes each from the digit shapes at $58C2) through $589C.
Copies the 8-byte shape of digit $0A00+X from $58C2 to the pointer $85/$86 and moves the pointer on 8 bytes.
The shapes of the digits 0 to 9, 8 bytes each (80 bytes).
The shapes of the digits 8 and 9 (16 bytes, 8 a digit), the last two of digit_shapes ($58C2). Each row is one byte of four two-bit pixels, of which the last is blank in these two digits.

The player's state: 1 standing or walking, 2 falling, 3 jumping, 4 climbing, 5 punching, 6 crouching, 7 a strike or hop with a short arc. Chosen by the routine for the current state and read by $5925, by $6111 and by the strike and jump routines ($5AEC, $5F5B).
Table of the eight state routines, one word each: 0 $5950 (an RTS), 1 $5BBC, 2 $5D8F, 3 $5E9E, 4 $600B, 5 $59E0, 6 $5B31, 7 $5A3E.
The high bytes of the words of the player state table at $5913 (every second byte).

The player's X ($747B) before this frame's move; put back when the move would end inside a solid tile. The scroll code $206C also saves the X here ($208B) and its scroll routines put it back ($2181, $34D7) when they undo a scroll step.
The player's Y ($747C) before this frame's move, saved by $5925. The scroll code $206C also saves the Y here ($2091), and its scroll routines put it back ($26DF, $2A78) when they undo a scroll step.

Called from $6480 each frame, unless the banner flag $56D1 or the wipe flag $74BA is set. Unless the game is paused ($6443) it saves the player position in $5923/$5924 and runs the routine for the player's state $5912 (table at $5913, through a call whose operand is rewritten at $5948/$5949); it then draws the player's frames with $6111, paused or not.
operand $5948/$5949 rewritten from the table at $5913; $5BBC shown is the value left in the file
Low byte of the address in the JSR at $5947, rewritten by $593E with the routine for the current case, so the call goes to a different routine each time.
High byte of the address in the JSR at $5947, rewritten by $5944 with the routine for the current case, so the call goes to a different routine each time.
Scratch of $7401: the world X, low byte, then the world height, low byte.
Scratch of $7401: the world X, high byte, then the world height, high byte.
A lone RTS, the routine of player state 0, which does nothing.
Index of the current walk or climb frame, stepped by $5977, $5998 and the climb code.
The 18 sprite pointer values of the left-facing walk, three for each of six poses.
The 18 sprite pointer values of the right-facing walk.
Toggled by $5977 and $5998, and by the climb routines $5FC9 and $5FEA, so that the walk or climb frame index advances every second call.
Steps the left-facing walk animation: toggles $5976 and, on every other call, advances the index $5951 through the 18 frames at $5952, and on every call puts the frame in $610D.
The same for the right-facing walk: advances $5951 and takes the frame from the 18 at $5964.
1 when the player faces left, 0 when he faces right.
The tile column under the player, kept by $5BBC at $5C75 for the climb test at $5C96.
Sets the three frame numbers in $610E-$6110 for the punch: $90, $B4, $BE facing right, $91, $B5, $BF facing left.

Player state 5, punching. While the timer $5BBA is non-zero it counts it down each frame and sets the punch frames through $59BB. When it has run out the state holds until fire is released, then returns to state 1 with the punch delay $5B2F set to 6.
Sets the three frame numbers in $610E-$6110 for the strike: $8C, $A3, $B0 facing right and $8D, $B1, $BB facing left.
Table of the 13 height steps of state 7, 16-bit values: -6 to +6.

Player state 7: adds the 13 signed steps of the table at $5A24 (-6 up to +6) to his height in turn and moves him 2 pixels a frame the way he faces ($59B9), without reading the joystick. It sets the strike frames through $59FF while the timer $5B2C runs and returns to state 1 when the steps are used up or, from the eighth step on, when he lands on a solid tile.

Set to 10 by $5A3E and by $5E9E when the strike timer $5B2C counts down to zero, and counted down by both while that timer is zero; nothing else reads it. State 7 ends after at most 13 frames and zeroes the timer itself, so the setting to 10 seems never to happen.
Frames left of the strike, set to $0E when a strike starts ($5B44 from the crouch, $5D10 from $5BBC) and counted down by $5A3E and $5E9E; the hit test $10B2, the draw routine $6111 and $6444 read it.
Set to 1 when the player is crouching; read by $5507 and $6111.
Delay before the player can crouch or strike again: set to 10 when a strike or a crouch ends, to 4 when a climb ends and to 0 when a jump ends, and counted down by $5CF1.
Frames before the next punch can start, set to 6 when a punch ends and counted down by $5D3D.
Delay before the next jump, counted down by $5BBC.

Player state 6, crouching. Fire starts the strike (state 7, timer $5B2C set to $0E, sound effect 0 through $B0EE). Down held keeps him crouched and turns him with left and right; letting go of down returns to state 1.
Holds the Y register saved by $5B4D: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5B55, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $5B4A: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5B57, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Sets the three frame numbers in $610E-$6110 for the crouch: $92, $B6, $C0 facing right, $93, $B7, $C1 facing left.
Frames left of the punch, set to 9 when it starts and counted down by $59E0; the hit test $10B2, the draw routine $6111 and $6444 read it.
Read at $5CD7 to stop a climb down from starting; nothing writes it in this file.

Player state 1, standing and walking. Counts down the jump delay $5B30, clears the hit flags and $5B2C, then moves 2 pixels left or right from the stored joystick $2064 (bits 2 and 3), unless $796D or $79D6 blocks it or he is at the map's end (world X below $2A or from $396), and keeps him out of solid tiles through the map pointer from $7401. The tile under his feet decides what comes next: an empty tile, $12 or one above $12 starts a fall (state 2); up on a $12 or $13 tile starts a climb (4), up otherwise a jump (3) once $5B30 is zero; down on a $10 or $11 tile starts a climb down (4); otherwise, once the delay $5B2E is zero, down with fire starts the strike (7) and down alone crouches (6); fire starts a punch (5) once $5B2F is zero.
Holds the Y register saved by $5D19: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5D21, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $5D16: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5D23, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the Y register saved by $5D5E: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5D66, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $5D5B: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5D68, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Puts the standing frame in $610D: $9A when the player faces right, $A0 when he faces left.

Player state 2, falling. Moves left and right from the joystick as in state 1, then lowers him 3 pixels a frame (2 from line $82, none from $97) until the tile below is solid, which sets state 1. Shows frame $7A or $7B by the facing.
Puts the falling frame in $610D: $7A when the player faces right and $7B when he faces left.
Table of the 39 height steps of the jump, 16-bit values, two bytes each, used by $5E9E through $5E9C: from -4 at the start through 0 to +4 at the end.
Index into the jump or strike height tables ($5E4E, $5A24), two bytes a step.
When non-zero, the state $6111 draws this frame instead of $5912 (set to 1, 3, 6 or 0 by the state changes in $5BBC and $5E9E); cleared by $6111 after use.

Player state 3, a jump. Adds the 39 signed steps of the table at $5E4E (rising and then falling, two bytes each) to the height $747C, steers left and right from the joystick, shows the jump frames and returns to state 1 when the table ends or the player lands.
Puts the jump frame in $610D: $F8 facing right, $F9 facing left.
1 while the player climbs up and 0 while he climbs down; read by $600B at the end of a climb.
Twelve sprite pointer values of the climb upwards ($94 to $96), indexed by $5951.
Twelve sprite pointer values of the climb downwards, indexed by $5951.
Advances the climb frame upwards: toggles $5976 and, on every other call, steps $5951 through 12, and on every call puts the frame from the table at $5FB1 in $610D.
Advances the climb frame downwards: toggles $5976 and, on every other call, steps $5951 through 12, and on every call puts the frame from the table at $5FBD in $610D.

Player state 4, climbing. Sets the jump delay $5B30 to 10, moves him up one pixel (up held, bit 0 clear, with the frames from $5FC9) or down one (down held, bit 1 clear, frames from $5FEA), and goes back to state 1 with the standing frame when the tile below his feet is not one of $10 to $13.
Fills with $FF the entries of the sorted sprite list at $0010 that each of the 11 slots used last frame (their positions are in $02-$0C).

Turns the 11 slots' world positions into screen positions for sprites 3-7 and sorts them by height. For each slot, X from $0A down, it subtracts the camera ($FB-$FE) to get the screen position ($87,X and $BF,X across, $A3,X and $DB,X down); a slot that is off the screen gets position 0, otherwise its number is put at the first free place from height/2 in the list at $0010. Writes $64 in $78 as the list end.
Sprite pointer value of the player's main frame, set by the state routines from the frame tables ($5952, $5964 and others) by the facing.
Sprite pointer value for the player's sprite 2 (the third, pointers $CFFA/$CBFA) when the punch, strike or crouch frames are in use, set by $59BB, $59FF and $5B95.
Sprite pointer value for the player's first sprite when the punch, strike or crouch frames are in use.
Sprite pointer value for the player's sprite 1 (the second, pointers $CFF9/$CBF9) when the punch, strike or crouch frames are in use.

Writes the player's three sprite pointers into both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFA and $CBF8-$CBFA) from the frame numbers in $610D-$6110, with different arrangements for states 2-4 and for the punch, crouch and strike.

Called by the hit test $10B2 with X the slot and Y the object. Takes 2 (when $10B1 is set) or 1 from the object's energy $0BA5 and adds 4 to the score digit 5; at zero energy it sets the slot and object to state $10, $0B00 to $FE and adds 8 to the score digit 5.
Holds the X register saved by $61CE: the immediate operand of the LDX at $61D8, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
Holds the X register saved by $61EE: the immediate operand of the LDX at $61F8, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.
The 30 sprite pointer values of a knocked-down enemy of variant 0, indexed by the phase $0A6A in behaviour $6273.
The 30 sprite pointer values for the following sprite of a knocked-down enemy of variant 0, read by $1D3E.
The 30 sprite pointer values of a knocked-down enemy of variant 1, indexed by the phase $0A6A in behaviour $6273.
The 30 sprite pointer values for the following sprite of a knocked-down enemy of variant 1, read by $1D3E.

Behaviour for state 16, probably an enemy that has been beaten down. $0B00 (set to $FE by $61AC) counts down; the frame follows a ramp up and down through the tables at $61FB and $6237 (by the variant flag $0BF8) with the phase in $0A6A. At zero the object gets energy 3 in $0BA5 and returns to the state saved in $0AFF (minus $0D when that is 3 or more), through $0A94 and $0AA2.
Sets the screen matrix bits of $D018 to $30 (screen at $CC00) when $2067 is zero and to $20 ($C800) when it is not, keeping the other bits.

Raster interrupt 2 of 3, on line $C5 (set by $6480). Moves sprites 3-7 to line $0A and clears all eight sprite pointers in both screens, turns sprites off, sets $D018 and $D011 for the panel with extended colour mode, counts down $5577 and $1658, reads $DC00 (joystick port 2) into $2064 and $DC01 (port 1 and the keyboard) into $2065 unless the recoil counter $1658 is running while $5577 is zero, sets the character set bits of $D018 to 8, runs the countdown $759B and the list clear $6088, toggles $63E7 and counts $63E6 down every second frame. It sets line $CD and the vector $63E8 for the next interrupt.
Holds the interrupted program's A register: stored here by $6315 on entry and reloaded by the LDA at $63DF before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDA at $63DF).
Holds the interrupted program's X register: stored here by $6318 on entry and reloaded by the LDX at $63E1 before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDX at $63E1).
Holds the interrupted program's Y register: stored here by $631B on entry and reloaded by the LDY at $63E3 before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDY at $63E3).
Counted down every second frame by $6315 while it is not zero; nothing else in this file reads it.
Toggled every frame by $6315.

Raster interrupt 3 of 3, on line $CD (set by $6315). Sets bitmap mode in $D011 and multicolour in $D016, with a run of NOPs timing the writes, then sets line 0 and the vector $6480, turns extended colour mode off, runs $206C unless the banner flag $56D1 is set, and restores A, X and Y from the operands at $643D-$6441.
Holds the interrupted program's A register: stored here by $63E8 on entry and reloaded by the LDA at $643C before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDA at $643C).
Holds the interrupted program's X register: stored here by $63EB on entry and reloaded by the LDX at $643E before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDX at $643E).
Holds the interrupted program's Y register: stored here by $63EE on entry and reloaded by the LDY at $6440 before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDY at $6440).
1 while the game is paused ($2029); the interrupts skip the moving parts while it is set. Also set by the wipe $74BC.
Moves sprite 0 or sprite 1 by 8 pixels along X while the punch timer $5BBA or the strike timer $5B2C runs, to the right when the player faces right ($59B9 zero) and to the left otherwise.

Raster interrupt 1 of 3, on line 0 (the line is written by $63E8). Saves A, X and Y in the operands at $6553-$6558 (restored by the LDA, LDX and LDY there), takes the fine scrolls $2061 into $D016 and $2062 into $D011, selects the screen buffer through $62FF, and sets the sprite multicolours. With $56D1 set it runs only the banner $55A1 and then sets the next interrupt; otherwise it sorts the sprites ($60B7) and, unless the wipe flag $74BA is set, multiplexes sprites 3-7 ($6604), runs the player ($5925), places sprites 0-2 at the player ($747B,$747C) and sets their colours. It then runs the sound-effect driver's play $B176 (at $6526), the multiplexer again, the colour copy ($69E3) and the object update ($1214), and sets line $C5 and the vector $6315 in $FFFE/$FFFF.
Holds the interrupted program's A register: stored here by $6480 on entry and reloaded by the LDA at $6553 before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDA at $6553).
Holds the interrupted program's X register: stored here by $6483 on entry and reloaded by the LDX at $6555 before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDX at $6555).
Holds the interrupted program's Y register: stored here by $6486 on entry and reloaded by the LDY at $6557 before the RTI (the immediate operand of the LDY at $6557).
Busy-wait: the outer count is A and the inner count is A as well (X and Y both start from A), so the callers' $14 to $FF give delays from a few milliseconds to about a third of a second.
The colour that colour_cycle ($6574) takes from cycle_colours_a ($6564) for the current step. It is 0 in the snapshot, and no traced code reads it.
Eight colours for one step of colour_cycle ($6574): white, light grey, mid grey, dark grey, black, then dark grey, mid grey and light grey again. The routine copies the entry for the step to $6563.
Eight colours for one step of colour_cycle ($6574): white, cyan, light blue, blue, black, then blue, light blue and cyan again. The routine copies the entry for the step to $65A4.

Steps a three-colour cycle on every fourth call: while the counter $65A3 is not 0 it takes 1 off and returns; at 0 it sets the counter to 3, moves the step $65A2 on by 1 (back to 0 at 8) and copies the entries for the step from cycle_colours_a to $6563, from cycle_colours_b to $65A4 and from cycle_colours_c to $65A5. No traced code calls or jumps to it, and nothing reads the three bytes it writes.
Four variables of colour_cycle ($6574), all 0 in the snapshot: the step 0 to 7 ($65A2), the call counter ($65A3), and the colours it copies from cycle_colours_b ($65A4) and cycle_colours_c ($65A5).
Eight colours for one step of colour_cycle ($6574): brown, orange, light red, yellow, white, then yellow, light red and orange again. The routine copies the entry for the step to $65A5.

Mixes CIA 1's timer A, both bytes, with the previous result in $65CD and rotates it: a random number in A and $65CD. The low three bits of $DC04 are written into the offset of the branch at $65BE (at $65BF), which sets how many of the rotates at $65C0 are run.
The offset of the branch at $65BE, rewritten by $65B3 with the low three bits of CIA 1 timer A so that the random number routine rotates a different number of times on each call.
The last random number: the seed of $65AE and its result.

Starts with RTS, so it returns at once. The bytes after it (not traced) would read CIA 2 port A bit 2 and, when it is clear, pull three bytes off the stack and jump to $0810; nothing reaches them while the RTS is there.
Fills the 1 KB screen matrix at $CC00-$CFFF with A.
Fills colour RAM $D800-$DBFF with A.
Index into the sprite list at $0010 of the last slot the multiplexer handled.
Raster line limit for the multiplexer: $26 for the first pass, $8C for the second.

Sprite multiplexer for sprites 3 to 7, called from $6480 up to twice a frame: at $64E7, which is skipped while the wipe flag $74BA is set, and at $6533; neither call runs while the banner flag $56D1 is set. Takes the next slot from the list at $0010 (from the index in $6602), and, while the raster line is below the limit in $6603, gives it the next of the five sprites whose previous slot has finished (its height $15 lines or more above the raster): height into $D007, $D009, $D00B, $D00D or $D00F, X with its ninth bit in $D010, the pointer into both screens' tables ($CFFB-$CFFF and $CBFB-$CBFF), the colour from $0A40 and the multicolour bit from $0A4E.
Twelve bytes: the single-bit masks $04, $08, $10, $20, $40 and $80 (the bits of sprites 2 to 7), then the same bits inverted: $FB, $F7, $EF, $DF, $BF and $7F. No traced code reads them.
Set by $6809 when part of the colour RAM is still to be copied from $7173; read and cleared by $69E3, and cleared by the level setup at $539C.

Sets the flag $6808 and copies the colours from the buffer at $7123-$7171 to colour RAM $D990-$D9DE, leaving out column 39 of both rows ($714A and $7172), the first half of the update that $69E3 finishes in the next interrupt.

When the flag $6808 is set, clears it and copies the colours from the buffer at $7173-$7289 to colour RAM $D9E0-$DAF6, leaving out column 39 of every row (the buffer ends at row 18, column 38). The second half of the colour update that $6809 starts.
Copies the colour byte at $721F into colour RAM at $DA8C; named only so that colour_copy_b's 1,024-byte reach covers it.
The second half of the unrolled copy that starts at $69E3: the colours from $7220 on, to colour RAM $DA8D and up to $DAF6.
Picks the colour builder for the screen matrix in use: $465E when $2067 is 0, else $3A06. Nothing in the level calls it; $334A and the other scroll phases make the same choice themselves.
Fills colour RAM for screen rows 0 to 9, columns 0 to $28, through the colour table at $BF00, from the matrix being built (the one at $C800 when $2067 is 0, otherwise $CC00).

Table of 16-bit pointers to the map rows, one two-byte entry for each row starting at $7A40 with 64 bytes to the row (the first row has two entries, so entry n points at row n-1); indexed at $7470 by the height ($FD/$FE less $AE plus $747C) divided by 8 and made even.

Works out where the player stands on the map: the world X from the camera and $747B (stored in $1FC2/$1FC3), the tile column from it in Y (divided by 16, less 1), and the map row pointer from the table at $7303, indexed by the camera's height plus $747C, into $E9/$EA. Writes the continue screen's texts at $CD49 and $CF8C, adding $66 to each character code and turning $20 into 0, and then the digits of $0A12 and $8C8B at $CF94 and $CE1C.
The countdown shown on the continue screen, set to 9 and counted down by $8CBC; read by $8C40 and by $8CBC at $8D42.
Set to 1 by $903A when the briefing has ended; nothing reads it in this file.

Set to 1 by $8CBC when fire is pressed to continue; read by the main loop at $2003.

The continue screen, entered from the main loop when the player has no energy left and $0A12 is not zero. Sets up the text screen, clears the score, draws "PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" and "CREDITS" with the digits through $8C40 and counts the digit in $8C8B down from 9 with delays; fire sets $8CBB to 1 and takes one from $0A12, and when the count runs out the level is not restarted.

The game over screen: runs the wipe $74BC, silences the sound ($B828), sets the text screen, swaps the character shapes ($8FFF), clears the screen and fills colour RAM with 9, writes "GAME OVER" from $8E02 at $CD50, waits through six long delays, puts the shapes back ($8FFF), clears the screen and redraws the panel ($54D6).
"GAME OVER" in screen codes, ended by $FF; written by $8D6C with $66 added to each code.
136 bytes of character shapes that $8FFF swaps with the block at $C338.

The last nine of the 17 character shapes of text_shapes_a ($8E0C), 8 bytes each: the characters $6F to $77, which the screen codes 9 to 17 (I to Q) reach with $66 added. $8FFF swaps them into the character set at $C378.
136 bytes of character shapes that $8FFF swaps with the block at $C3C0.

The last nine of the 17 character shapes of text_shapes_b ($8E94), 8 bytes each: the characters $80 to $88. $80 is the letter Z (screen code 26 with $66 added) and $81 a full stop, the stop code $1B that the briefing at $90CE uses (the game over text at $8E02 has none). The others are punctuation that those two texts do not use: $82 looks like a colon, $83 like a short opening bracket, $84 an equals sign, $85 a question mark, $86 a bar and $87 an exclamation mark, and $88 is blank. $8FFF swaps them into the character set at $C400.
Key code read by $8F45 and stored by $2127; cleared to 0 by the continue screen ($8CEE) and the game over screen ($8D96). $50 pauses, $20 can end the level.

Reads the keyboard with CIA 1 into A. Returns $FF at once when any of the low five bits of $DC00 AND $DC01 reads low (the test at $8F4D, so while the joystick or a key in that range is down); otherwise scans the eight rows from $8F5B, looks the key up in the table at $8FBF and returns its code. $2127 keeps the result in $8F44.
The row select value written to $DC00 by $8F45 while it scans the keyboard, rotated one bit for each row.
The number of the keyboard row $8F45 is scanning.
The column bits from $DC01 still to be tested for the row being scanned by $8F45, saved shifted by $8F87 when a key is found and reloaded at $8FB0 to go on testing when that key has no code.
Key codes for the 64 keys of the matrix, indexed by 8 times the column plus the row; $80 and above mean no code. Read by $8F45.

Exchanges three blocks: 136 bytes at $8E0C and 136 at $8E94 with $C338 and $C3C0, and the 80 bytes of digit shapes at $58C2 with $C450. Called to put the text screens' shapes in and to restore the play shapes.

Counter of $903A: the passes of the typing loop still to run before a press of fire is accepted, from $1E; a line end takes a pass as a character does, so fire is first tested after 29 characters of the briefing.
The index of the next character of the briefing text at $90CE, kept by $903A.

Types the level briefing at $90CE on the screen one character at a time (screen pointer from $CC56, lines 80 apart, a delay of $32 before each character), after a delay of $14 and clearing the screen and colour RAM (colour 7). Fire is ignored for the first 30 passes of the loop (29 characters and the first line end) and ends the typing after that; when the text is done it waits for fire. Sets $8C8C to 1 and waits through two long delays.
Holds the Y register saved by $9070: the immediate operand of the LDY at $9078, reloaded after the call or table lookup that follows.

Characters 0 to 127 of the play character set (1,024 bytes, 8 bytes a character, one byte a pixel row). The playfield's top part shows screen A or B in text mode with the character base at $D000 ($D018 low nibble 4); tile_top_chars ($9651) and tile_bottom_chars ($96EF) pick the codes, and char_colours ($BF00) gives each its colour. Only the VIC sees these bytes: with the I/O area switched in, the CPU reads the chips' registers at the same addresses.

Characters 128 to 239 of the play character set (896 bytes), the same form as play_charset_a. The map's tiles put codes up to $ED on the screen ($EE and $EF only in tile $3B, which the map does not use). Only the VIC sees these bytes: with the I/O area switched in, the CPU reads the chips' registers at the same addresses.

Characters 240 to 255 (128 bytes), all zero: the blank characters. The tile tables hold $F0 to $F6 and $F8 (top rows) and $F9 to $FF (bottom rows) only for tiles $3C to $3F, which the map does not use. Sprite pointers $5E and $5F would read the same bytes, and pointers $5A to $5D read characters 208 to 239 as sprite data, so $5A to $5F are not shapes.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $60 and $61 (128 bytes): the two frames of the hazard of behaviour $1E06, named by hazard_frames ($1DFA). They look like a burst of light.
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $62 and $63 (128 bytes): the pickup of behaviour $1ADD, named by pickup_frames_a ($1ACF). A small heart, then a larger one.
Sprite shapes for pointers $64 to $66 (192 bytes): three flames of growing height, shown in turn by the hazard of behaviour $1C1C (hazard_arc_steps at $1CD1, where a value of $5A or more is a frame).

Sprite shape for pointer $67 (64 bytes): a small round spark, the shot of behave_shooter ($14F4), and the frame the hazard of behaviour $1C1C shows while it flies: $1C2E sets it on every call, and only the steps of hazard_arc_steps that hold a frame ($5A or more) replace it.
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $68 and $69 (128 bytes): the shuttling object of behaviour $1457, named by shuttle_frames ($1448).

Sprite shapes for pointers $6A to $6C (192 bytes). $6A and $6B look like two guns, shown by behave_prop_flash ($1C01): $6B while its counter runs and $6A otherwise. $6C looks like a muzzle flash, the first frame of the hazard arc table (hazard_arc_steps at $1CD1).
Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $6D to $6F (192 bytes): a row of spikes at three heights, named by anim_frames ($1596), the animated hazard of behaviour $15F2.
Sprite shape for pointer $70 (64 bytes): a case with a cross on it. No table or constant of level 2 names it.
Sprite shape for pointer $71 (64 bytes): a small flame, a frame of the hazard of behaviour $1C1C (hazard_arc_steps at $1CD1).

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $75 to $79 (320 bytes): a disc seen at five angles, the pickup of behaviour $1BAF, named by pickup_frames_b ($1B96).

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $7A to $7F (384 bytes): the player falling. fall_frame ($5E3B) sets the pose to $7A or $7B and player_draw adds 2 and 4 for the other two sprites, so the pointers are $7A, $7C, $7E and $7B, $7D, $7F.

Sprite shapes for pointers $80 to $8F (1,024 bytes). $80 to $85 are the third sprite of the player standing or walking right and $86 to $8B of the player standing or walking left: player_draw ($6111) writes F - $17 to $CFFA, with F from walk_frames_right, walk_frames_left or stand_frame. frame_b ($610E) takes $8C and $8D from strike_frames. Sprite shapes for pointers $94 to $96 (192 bytes): the player climbing, picked by climb_frames_up ($5FB1) and climb_frames_down ($5FBD). In the climbing state player_draw writes F, F + $24 and F + $2E to $CFFA, $CFF8 and $CFF9, so the other two sprites are $B8 to $BA and $C2 to $C4.

Sprite shapes for pointers $97 to $9C (384 bytes): the player walking right (walk_frames_right at $5964). When he stands or walks, player_draw shows three sprites with the pointers F ($CFF8), F + $0D ($CFF9) and F - $17 ($CFFA): $A4 to $A9 and $80 to $85 for these. Falling and jumping use F, F + 2 and F + 4 instead.
Sprite shapes for pointers $9D to $A2 (384 bytes): the player walking left (walk_frames_left at $5952), drawn like walk_right_shapes, with $AA to $AF and $86 to $8B as the other two sprites.

The bytes of $B2 are the same in the level 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 listings, and its top rows are those of $FA, a jump shape, one row lower, so it looks like an unused variant of it.
